paper.title: Randomized Greedy Learning for Non-monotone Stochastic Submodular Maximization Under Full-bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Unconstrained stochastic combinatorial MAB with non-monotone submodular-in-expectation reward under full-bandit feedback
unmapped: Action set is all subsets of n base arms (unconstrained, no cardinality limit)
Reward function is submodular in expectation, not necessarily monotone; realizations need not be submodular
Regret is 1/2-approximation regret: compared against (1/2) E f(OPT)
Full-bandit feedback: only joint reward of the chosen set observed
settings.definition_quote: We assume the reward function $f(\cdot)$ to be stochastic and submodular in expectation, see Definition \ref{def:submod}, not necessarily monotone, and i.i.d. conditioned on a given subset. Without loss of generality, we assume $f(\cdot)$ to be bounded in $[0,1]$ ... $\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}_{\frac{1}{2}}] = \frac{1}{2}T \mathbb{E} [f(OPT)] - \sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}[f(S_t)]$

conditions: reward function submodular in expectation (not necessarily monotone)

source.quote: For the sequential decision making problem defined in Section \ref{problem} with $T \geq 2$, the expected cumulative $\frac{1}{2}$-regret of RGL is at most $\mathcal{O}(n T^{\frac{2}{3}} \log(T)^{\frac{1}{3}})$.

results.notes: Alpha-regret with alpha=1/2, defined through expected values, hence pseudo_regret. O(1) per-round time. Remark 3 notes an anytime version via doubling trick with the same rate up to constants (not formally stated).
